question: Which of the randomness sources named by nix-hermit-execbuilder-prototype_20260729 actually leak under `hermit run --no-namespace`, by what mechanism, and is --no-namespace required for the Nix execBuilder seam at all?
headline: `hermit run --tmp=/tmp` (an existing flag) determinizes all five measured sources AND keeps guest writes visible on the host, under both host /tmp and paths outside it. --no-namespace was never required: the obstacle was Hermit's private /tmp tmpfs, not the mount namespace. AT_RANDOM and /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid were already determinized in every mode. getpid() is the sole primitive leak of --no-namespace, and bash $RANDOM is its intermittent observable consequence. No Hermit code change is required.

host.note: AMD; ARCH_SET_CPUID returns ENODEV (no CPUID faulting) and PMU validation reports AmdSpecLockMapShouldBeDisabled. Neither affects these probes: none reads CPUID or RDTSC, and all modes are measured on the same host.

hermit.delta_vs_base: one commit, confined to `run_sabre` in hermit-cli/src/lib.rs (SaBRe backend). Unreachable from the ptrace backend used for every measurement here, so it cannot affect these results.

method.recorded_quantity: number of DISTINCT values observed across the N runs of one (source, mode) cell
method.verdict_rule: distinct == 1 => determinized; distinct > 1 => LEAK; write probes report visible / DISCARDED
method.relaxations: none beyond the mode under test; the mode IS the variable
method.positive_control: the `native` mode must report LEAK on all five randomness sources, proving each probe can detect variation; it does (10 distinct / 10 runs on every source)
method.usability_control: the two write probes make a mode's verdict meaningful: a mode that determinizes but discards the build directory does not solve the problem
method.guest_env: LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC exported by the harness

command: cd harness && cc -O2 -o probes probes.c && N=10 HERMIT_BIN=<hermit> ./run-matrix.sh
recommendation: Nix execBuilder wrapper should use `hermit run --tmp=/tmp` instead of `setarch -R hermit run --no-namespace`. setarch -R is unnecessary because the full-namespace mode pins ASLR itself.

supersedes_claims.claim: default (full namespace) mode does not persist writes to $out; 'private mnt ns discards them'
supersedes_claims.verdict: REFUTED — writes outside /tmp are visible on the host under the default mode. Only /tmp is discarded, because Hermit mounts a private tmpfs there; with `sandbox = false` Nix's build directory lives under /tmp, which is what actually vanished.

supersedes_claims.claim: AT_RANDOM-seeded userspace PRNGs are not virtualized under --no-namespace; bash $RANDOM differs because it derives from AT_RANDOM
supersedes_claims.verdict: REFUTED — AT_RANDOM is byte-identical across 10 runs in every mode measured

supersedes_claims.claim: /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid is read straight from the host kernel RNG under --no-namespace
supersedes_claims.verdict: REFUTED — identical across 10 runs; Hermit intercepts the path via ProcfsKind::RandomUuid

supersedes_claims.claim: the procfs UUID probe is determinized under --no-namespace
supersedes_claims.verdict: CONFIRMED, and shown not to depend on rootless podman — it reproduces on the bare host

supersedes_claims.claim: bash seeds $RANDOM from the real host getpid()
supersedes_claims.verdict: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — getpid is measured to be the only varying seed input, but the bash-internal seed path is NOT verified; a reimplementation of bash 5.1's documented seedrand/intrand32 did not reproduce the observed triples

limitations: The bash-internal path from getpid() to $RANDOM is inferred by elimination, not confirmed against this bash build's source or a debugger.
Only the ptrace backend was measured. KVM, DBI, SaBRe, LiteInst and e9patch were not exercised.
Single host; run-to-run stability only. Cross-host reproducibility of the determinized values was not tested.
N=10 per randomness cell. A source varying with probability below ~10% per run could read as determinized; bash_random measured 3/10 in one block and 5/10 in another, showing that regime is real.
Write visibility is N=1 per mode: it is a deterministic filesystem property, not a sampled one.
No Nix build was run. The recommendation follows from the measured flag semantics, not from a green nixpkgs derivation; validating a real target is the Nix agent's seam.
`--tmp=/tmp` shares host /tmp, which re-admits host state as a build input. Hermit determinizes execution, not a mutable shared filesystem.
